title: Technician Preparation and Source-Control for Indoor Air Quality Monitoring: Proposal of a Preliminary Precautionary Framework
content: Indoor air quality (IAQ) directly impacts occupant health, particularly for individuals with asthma, migraines, or multiple chemical sensitivity (MCS). Emerging research has identified humans as sources of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions, highlighting the need for greater investigation of sampling conditions and human-associated VOC sources. While technical IAQ testing protocols, such as those provided by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Health Canada, and ASHRAE, provide guidance for sampling, they do not address technician-related sources of VOCs. Personal products, laundering, smoking, and fragrances emit VOCs and can persist on clothing and skin that may be reflected in IAQ sampling. Although fragrance-free alternatives reduce VOC emissions, such technician-related source-control measures are not consistently documented in IAQ testing, representing a potential gap in IAQ quality assurance. This paper examines IAQ testing protocols used in Canadian office buildings, synthesizing evidence on human pollutant sources, and susceptibility of vulnerable populations, while proposing a preliminary precautionary framework for technician preparation, informed by operational experience, to minimize technician-related VOC emissions during IAQ sampling. This paper aims to provide a foundation for future evaluation of technician-related VOC contamination during IAQ monitoring and to support environmental health decision-making. The proposed precautionary measures are informed by VOC literature and practical experience rather than experimental validation and are presented as a preliminary framework for future research aimed at improving environmental monitoring and assessment methods.
